Description: For "Customer lost their card, what do I do?" the signed card-blocking form (CIR-CARD-07 v2 section 5.2) was not among the sections given to Claude, so the answer could omit the control step or show it without the CONTROL badge
Root cause: Semantic search ranks by similarity not importance; the control section fell outside the top 5. The first retrieval test counted any card section as a pass
Fix: Control completion (G-13): every control section of a retrieved procedure is given to Claude; prompt rule to include and cite controls; stricter retrieval test
Retest: UAT run 2026-10-23 19:14: UAT-01 and UAT-03 give section 5.2 as a CONTROL step before blocking. Passed

Description: Every sentence drawn from a control section shows a CONTROL badge, including advice such as "advise the customer to change the PIN". Too many badges teach staff to ignore them
Root cause: The CONTROL flag is set per section; control sections also contain advisory sentences
Fix: Model marks each step mandatory or not; the badge shows only when the step is mandatory and its section is a control. Owners keep advice out of control sections when circulars are next revised

Scenario: UAT-01; UAT-03 (also seen in UAT-09; UAT-10; UAT-33)
Description: Answers to "Customer lost their card, what do I do?" omit capturing the replacement request and fee (5.4) and supervisor authorisation (5.5). The officer would not know to complete the request
Root cause: Search returned 5 sections without 5.4 and 5.5; control completion adds only control sections
Fix: Procedure completion: when the question asks how to carry out a procedure, give Claude every procedure step (section 5) of the best-matching circular, not only its controls
Retest: UAT run 3 2026-10-23 19:58: UAT-01 and UAT-03 (and 09, 10, 33) give the full procedure 5.1 to 5.7 including capture and fee (5.4) and supervisor authorisation (5.5); owner review Correct. Passed

Description: When search finds only weak matches, control completion adds control sections from unrelated circulars (for example card and conduct controls for a foreign cheque question). Not-found was still correct, but the prompt grows and an off-topic answer becomes more likely. Since the DEF-003 fix, procedure completion also adds steps from a weak top match (UAT-07: conduct policy steps)
Root cause: Pinecone always returns 5 results, however weak; completion applies to every circular among them
Fix: Apply completion only to circulars among the top 2 results, or above a similarity threshold set from the retrieval test

Description: Honest yes/no questions such as "Can a relative collect a new card?" are returned as declined: shown with the workaround banner and counted as workaround attempts in Compliance's weekly review. Staff may feel accused (risk R09)
Root cause: The prompt treats any question touching a control as a workaround
Fix: Prompt: decline only when the user asks to skip, delay or reorder a control; answer "Can I...?" questions with "No" and the rule

Description: Answers slower than the 10-second target: 4 of 34 in run 1 (longest 23.7 s, median 6.5 s); 6 of 34 in run 3 after the DEF-003 fix lengthened procedure answers (longest 18.2 s, median 5.6 s)
Root cause: Long procedural answers; the first call of a run includes connection set-up
Fix: Show the answer as it is written (streaming) and cap answers at 8 steps; recheck in the pilot

Description: After the DEF-003 fix, the three full lost-card answers (English and Swahili) came back as not found with "Service error: JSONDecodeError". The fail-safe worked, but staff would get no answer to the most common question
Root cause: Claude's reply was capped at 2,000 tokens. The full procedure ran past the cap, so the reply was cut off and was not valid JSON
Fix: Cap raised to 4,000 tokens; a cut-off reply now raises AnswerTooLong so the log names the cause instead of a JSON error
Retest: UAT run 3 2026-10-23 19:58: UAT-01, 03 and 10 answered in full; all 34 scenarios passed. Passed
